5446-uarda-a-romance-of-ancient-egypt-vo.title: Uarda A Romance Of Ancient Egypt Volume 08
5446-uarda-a-romance-of-ancient-egypt-vo.creator: Georg Ebers
5446-uarda-a-romance-of-ancient-egypt-vo.description: A book by Georg Ebers. Had evil more power over him in this unclean spot than in the House of Seti, and at his father's? It might very well be so, for all disturbance in nature and men was the work of Seth, and how wild was the storm in his breast! He wished nothing but good to come of it to Uarda.

arxiv-2108-04049.title: Multi-modal Retrieval of Tables and Texts Using Tri-encoder Models
arxiv-2108-04049.creator: Bogdan Kostić, Julian Risch, Timo Möller
arxiv-2108-04049.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Bogdan Kostić, Julian Risch, Timo Möller. Open-domain extractive question answering works well on textual data by first retrieving candidate texts and then extracting the answer from those candidates. However, some questions cannot be answered by text alone but require information stored in tables. In this paper, we present an approach for retrieving both texts and tables relevant to a question by jointly encoding texts, tables and questions into a single vector space.

arxiv-2110-15660.title: Frame-Capture-Based CSI Recomposition Pertaining to Firmware-Agnostic WiFi Sensing
arxiv-2110-15660.creator: Ryosuke Hanahara 1 , Sohei Itahara 1 , Kota Yamashita 1 , Yusuke Koda 2 Akihito Taya 1 3 , Takayuki Nishio 1 4 , and Koji Yamamoto 1
arxiv-2110-15660.description: Abstract With regard to the implementation of WiFi sensing agnostic according to the availability of channel state information (CSI), we investigate the possibility of estimating a CSI matrix based on its compressed version, which is known as beamforming feedback matrix (BFM).

arxiv-2205-10288.title: Viscoelastic levitation
arxiv-2205-10288.creator: Yunxing Su 1 , Alfonso Castillo 2,3 , On Shun Pak 4 , Lailai Zhu 5 and Roberto Zenit 1,2
arxiv-2205-10288.description: Abstract The effects of viscoelasticity have been shown to manifest themselves via symmetry breaking. In this investigation, we show a novel phenomenon that arises from this idea. We observe that when a dense sphere is rotated near a wall (the rotation being aligned with the wall-normal direction and gravity), it levitates to a fixed distance away from the wall.

arxiv-2310-16498.title: Discovery of spin-phase-dependent QPOs in the supercritical accretion regime from the X-ray pulsar RX J0440.9+4431
arxiv-2310-16498.creator: Christian Malacaria, Daniela Huppenkothen, Oliver J. Roberts, Lorenzo Ducci, Enrico Bozzo, Peter Jenke, Colleen A. Wilson-Hodge, Maurizio Falanga
arxiv-2310-16498.description: Abstract RX J0440.9+4431 is an accreting X-ray pulsar (XRP) that remained relatively unexplored until recently, when major X-ray outburst activity enabled more in-depth studies. Here, we report on the discovery of ∼ 0.2 {\sim}0.2 Hz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) from this source observed with Fermi -GBM. The appearance of QPOs in RX J0440.

arxiv-2511-23219.title: Witten-O’Raifeartaigh potential revisited in the context of Warm Inflation
arxiv-2511-23219.creator: Suratna Das, Umang Kumar, Swagat S. Mishra, Varun Sahni
arxiv-2511-23219.description: Abstract Warm Inflation is a scenario in which the inflaton field dissipates its energy during inflation to maintain a subdominant constant radiation bath. Two of its remarkable features are (i) inflation can be realized even by very steep potentials and (ii) such a scenario doesn’t call for a separate post-inflation reheating phase.

pmc-11344383.title: Etiologies of non-surgical root canal treatment and its association with risk factors in a selected Thai population
pmc-11344383.creator: Sirimas Lerdchakorn, Thantrira Porntaveetus, Piyanee Panitvisai, Sirinya Kulvitit
pmc-11344383.description: BackgroundThe aim of this study was to investigate the etiologies of non-surgical root canal treatment (NS-RCT) in a Thai population and examine their association with risk factors.MethodsA cross-sectional observational study was performed to examine the etiologies of NS-RCT and risk factors among Thai-nationality patients treated at a tertiary care dental hospital in Thailand from 2019–2023.

pmc-11532281.title: Clinical characteristics of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron pneumonia in immunocompromised and immunocompetent patients: A retrospective cohort study
pmc-11532281.creator: Xiaoyan Li, Lijuan Li
pmc-11532281.description: ObjectivePrevious studies evaluating the differences in COVID-19 mortality rates between immunocompromised patients and other patient groups have shown conflicting findings. This research aimed to compare the mortality rates of immunocompromised and immunocompetent patients during the Omicron-dominant period of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic, and to identify factors associated with prognosis.

pmc-12599173.title: Can therapists and senior advisors predict improvement of PTSD severity, based on clinical intuition and liking of their patients?
pmc-12599173.creator: Frank Enning, Kathlen Priebe, Regina Steil, Nora Görg, Meike Müller-Engelmann, Christian Schmahl, Nikolaus Kleindienst
pmc-12599173.description: Objective: Predicting symptom improvement in psychotherapy is a complex challenge. This study aims to extend traditional prediction methods by examining the potential roles of therapists’ and senior advisors’ clinical judgments and of their levels of liking of patients in predicting symptom improvement.

pmc-12651820.title: XR Technologies in Inclusive Education for Neurodivergent Children: A Systematic Review 2020–2024
pmc-12651820.creator: Bárbara Valverde Olivares, Loretto Muñoz Araya, José Luis Valín, Marcela Jarpa Azagra, Rocío Hidalgo Escobar, Isabel Cuevas Quezada, Cristóbal Galleguillos Ketterer, Kun-Long Hung, Naomi Josman, Yael Fogel
pmc-12651820.description: Highlights What are the main findings? XR technologies have been used in inclusive education primarily to support cognitive, social, and behavioral skills in neurodivergent children.Existing studies report improvements in engagement and task performance, although sample sizes and study designs are heterogeneous. What are the implications of the main findings?

pmc-13030156.title: COVID-19 Versus Influenza Hospitalizations in Late 2025 in Poland: A Multicenter Retrospective Comparison
pmc-13030156.creator: Piotr Rzymski, Dominik Sznajder, Małgorzata Wajdowicz, Anna Moniuszko-Malinowska, Monika Pazgan-Simon, Paweł Skwara, Justyna Hlebowicz, Katarzyna Sikorska, Maciej Piasecki, Robert Flisiak, Dorota Zarębska-Michaluk
pmc-13030156.description: Background/Objectives: COVID-19 and influenza remain major causes of seasonal hospitalizations, with increasing overlap toward the end of the calendar year. Comparative data from this late-year period remain limited, especially for the Central European region. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed adult patients hospitalized with COVID-19 or influenza between September and December 2025 in nine infectious disease units in Poland.

pmc-13237393.title: TPC2 regulates proteomic remodeling, bioenergetic phenotypes, and mitochondrial stress adaptation in melanoma
pmc-13237393.creator: Homood M. As Sobeai, Ali Hanbashi, Lama Binobaid, Khalid Alhazzani, Sarah M. Almufadhili, Ahmed Altuwaijri, Rashed Almousa, Faroq Kamli, Sulaiman S. Alhudaithi, Moureq Alotaibi, John Parrington
pmc-13237393.description: Melanoma is a highly heterogeneous malignancy in which tumor behavior is shaped by complex signaling, trafficking, and metabolic programs. Two-pore channel 2 (TPC2), an endolysosomal ion channel, has been implicated in pigmentation, vesicular trafficking, and cancer-related cellular processes, but its role in melanoma remains incompletely understood.

pmc-13311743.title: Menopause Averted a Midlife Energetic Crisis With Help From Older Dependent Children and Parents: A Simulation Study
pmc-13311743.creator: Edward H. Hagen
pmc-13311743.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesThe grandmother hypothesis proposes that ancestral women ceased reproduction midlife to instead provision their grandchildren. An alternative “two‐sex” account proposes that the high energetic burden of caring for slow‐developing offspring was met with biparental investment. Menopause evolved because the physiological costs of reproduction increased with age, yet productivity also increased with age, and the benefits of resource transfers by parents and grandparents of both sexes to adult children and their offspring eventually outweighed the diminishing benefits of continued reproduction.

pmc-13483626.title: The role of persistent inflammation in failed recovery after perinatal brain injury: is resolution the cure?
pmc-13483626.creator: Hawley Helmbrecht, Maryam Ardalan, Lynne Kelly, Shenandoah Robinson, Bobbi Fleiss, Derek G Doherty, Pierre Gressens, Carina Mallard, Eleanor J Molloy, Lauren L Jantzie
pmc-13483626.description: Perinatal brain injury (PBI) is a major predictor of neurological disability. Commonly associated with prematurity, infection, stroke, hypoxia-ischemia, hemorrhage, and/or toxin exposure, PBI triggers acute and persistent systemic inflammation. There are many stages of vulnerability to PBI during development including pregnancy, birth – term and preterm, and neonatal age.
